messages:
alex: FYI escalation from AcmeCorp via support ticket. They report intermittent 429s + high latency when sending bursts of concurrent generation requests. Customer says it only happens on model `redwood-4x` and only when context sizes are large (~11k tokens). They see 429s with `Retry-After` headers and occasional 503s. Ticket includes curl + response headers. Pasting summary below for triage.

maya: thanks — can you drop the customer's raw request/response sample here (sanitized keys) and their traffic pattern? i.e., requests/sec, concurrency, tokens per request.

alex: customer provided this snippet (sanitized):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-4x","input":"<~11k tokens payload>","max_tokens":512}'
```
and server response: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 24
x-rw-rate-limit-model: 45/60
x-rw-rate-limit-tenant: 120/300
Content-Type: application/json

{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"per-model RPM exceeded"}
```
Traffic pattern: they run bursts of ~20 concurrent requests for ~30s then idle for 2–3 mins. Average token volume per minute reported ~150k TPM during bursts.

sam: that header `x-rw-rate-limit-model: 45/60` looks like they hit a per-model rolling RPM metric (45 used out of 60 allowed). 20 concurrent requests each with a heavy context can push token throughput high even if RPM looks borderline. We should confirm the customer's API key, plan, and whether they're on Dedicated.

jordan: quick primer for context (helpful for support replies): model-level limits are enforced to protect serving capacity. Typical constraints we see: per-model RPM (requests/min) and TPM (tokens/min) caps, plus a concurrency cap which limits how many inflight requests for a single model an API key can have concurrently. Large contexts consume more token budget per request and also increase per-request latency (locks up compute for longer) — that leads to effective lower throughput and can trip rate-limiters sooner during bursts. Also if context > model context window it gets rejected/trimmed and may hit context-length throttle.

maya: do we have the exact default numbers for `redwood-4x` so we can tell the customer? need to avoid promising anything irreversible.

jordan: default for hosted tier (example): model RPM 60 req/min, model TPM 200k tokens/min, concurrency 10 inflight requests per key for that model. Note: enterprise/dedicated customers can have higher reserved capacity or per-key overrides. These defaults are examples — confirm in the admin console for the exact account.

alex: customer is on self-serve hosted (not Dedicated). their dashboard shows 60 RPM, 250k TPM quota at the tenant level, but model-specific throttle appears lower (dashboard shows model cap 60 RPM, 150k TPM for `redwood-4x`). that matches the `x-rw-rate-limit-model` header.

lia: billing note — if they want predictable throughput during bursts, upgrade path is either: 1) move to Dedicated, 2) request per-model limit increase (subject to capacity and review), or 3) purchase burst addon credits. Support should include these options.

sam: operational quick fixes we can recommend immediately: apply exponential backoff with jitter on 429s, limit client concurrency to <=8 for `redwood-4x` in their case, and pace requests so token/min doesn't spike above the model TPM. For long contexts, consider chunking or switching to a shorter prompt + retrieval pattern.

alex: customer also mentioned seeing slowness (1–2s additional latency) right before a 429. likely queueing/backpressure when too many heavy requests land — consistent with hitting concurrency/time-in-flight budget.

maya: let's provide repro steps they can run to confirm throttling source. Drafted: 1) run a single-thread loop creating 1 req/sec (small context) for 2 mins and note no 429s; 2) run 20 parallel processes each making 1 req/sec with 11k token context for 30s and observe 429s + `x-rw-rate-limit-model` dropping; 3) repeat but cap concurrency to 6 and verify errors go away. Include sample script.

alex: adding sample repro script for customer (shell + parallel):
```bash
# simple parallel tester (use with caution)
for i in $(seq 1 20); do 
  (while true; do \ 
    curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer ${API_KEY}" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"model":"redwood-4x","input":"<11k tokens>","max_tokens":0}' \
    sleep 0.1; done) &
done
# kill background procs after 30s
sleep 30; pkill -P $$
```

jordan: for engineering: please check autoscaler logs for `redwood-4x` around 2024-12-03T15:07Z (ticket timestamp) — we should verify if kernel selection or slow-path quantization added CPU/GPU latency that would reduce concurrency. Also check rate-limiter logs to see whether requests were dropped due to model-level token counters vs tenant-level.

sam: created infra job to pull rate-limiter traces and the serving pod CPU profiles for the window. ops-bot: job 8342 kicked off.

ops-bot: job 8342 started — collecting rate-limiter events and pod traces. ETA ~8m.

lia: support reply draft to customer: "You're hitting model-level rate limits because large contexts increase token consumption and per-request runtime, which, during bursts, causes the model's RPM/TPM and concurrency limits to be reached. Short-term mitigations: reduce concurrency/pace requests, implement backoff with jitter, or reduce context size. For a production fix we can discuss Dedicated capacity or a limit increase. We'll run traces and get back with exact numbers for your key."

maya: good. alex — once we get infra traces, please confirm whether it was model TPM exhaustion vs concurrency queueing. if it's concurrency we can consider increasing per-key inflight cap temporarily while telemetry is clean.

alex: acknowledged. will follow up with logs from ops job 8342 and then coordinate any temporary caps with product + infra.

sam: preliminary ops notes (will paste full output when ready): looks like during the 30s burst, model-serving median latency jumped from 220ms -> 1.1s and the rate-limiter shows token-debit spikes that exceed the model TPM window.

jordan: if the customer wants a code-level best practice to avoid this class of problem: 1) throttle client-side concurrency; 2) implement token-budgeting per minute (track tokens used per key); 3) use streaming RPC when possible to lower request blocking time; 4) if using retrieval-augmented generation with big contexts, do retrieval-first and only send top-k passage tokens.

alex: leaving open for infra results. will update thread with ops-bot trace when available. :thumbsup:
